title: Azure capstone -- putting the full stack together
exp: Ties every Azure day into the same end-to-end shape as the AWS capstone -- the question 'walk me through how this pipeline would look on Azure' should now have a confident, concrete answer.
pts: Full pipeline: source APIs -> Azure Data Factory (orchestration, ForEach fan-out) -> ADLS Gen2 raw landing zone -> Azure Databricks (validate + transform, job cluster) -> ADLS Gen2 processed zone (Delta/Parquet) -> Synapse serverless SQL (queryable layer) -> Grafana on Azure Monitor + Log Analytics (dashboard).

Identity story end to end: every hop uses Managed Identity with RBAC scoped to a Resource Group -- no connection strings or keys anywhere in the pipeline, mirroring the IAM-role-everywhere design principle from the AWS capstone.

Cost story: job clusters with autotermination, Synapse serverless's pay-per-query model, and Blob lifecycle rules moving cold data to cheaper tiers -- the same three cost levers (compute auto-shutdown, query-time cost control, storage tiering) as the AWS version, expressed through Azure-native mechanisms.

Observability story: Diagnostic Settings routing every resource's logs into one Log Analytics workspace, KQL-based alerts for the same conditions (no data in 25h, error rate > 5%, cluster idle), Grafana as the single pane of glass across Metrics and Logs.

The single best interview sentence for this whole track: 'The concepts transfer completely -- object storage, managed Spark, native monitoring, Terraform-managed infrastructure, Grafana as the visualization layer. What's genuinely different is the identity model (Managed Identity + RBAC scope instead of IAM roles + policy), the Resource Group as a cascading-delete container AWS doesn't have, and Synapse/ADF's more visual, less code-first design philosophy versus Athena/Step Functions.'

Config-driven design from the Domain track applies unchanged: each of the 50 sources is a parameter in the ADF pipeline's array input, not a hardcoded branch -- adding source 51 is a data change, not a pipeline redesign, exactly like the AWS Step Functions Map pattern.
pr: Draw the full Azure pipeline architecture diagram from memory, labeling each Azure service and its AWS equivalent

viz.cap: The complete Azure pipeline -- structurally identical to the AWS capstone, different vocabulary and identity model

qa.q: Walk through the full Azure-equivalent pipeline architecture end to end.
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** ADF triggers on a schedule, fans out 50 sources in parallel via ForEach, each fetching into an ADLS Gen2 raw landing zone. A Databricks job cluster validates and transforms the data, writing to a processed ADLS Gen2 zone in Delta/Parquet format. Synapse serverless SQL provides the queryable layer over that processed data, with CETAS pre-aggregating anything queried repeatedly. Diagnostic Settings route every resource's telemetry into one Log Analytics workspace, and Grafana on Azure Managed Grafana visualizes both Metrics and KQL-queried Logs on one dashboard, alerting on the same conditions as the AWS version -- silent source failure, elevated error rate, idle compute.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Window functions operate on a set of rows defined by the OVER() clause without collapsing them into a single row, allocating memory segments for frame calculation.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Partitioning over non-indexed columns with huge row counts forces expensive Sort operators and TempDB spills in execution plans.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Provides high readability and single-pass analytical aggregation, but can increase RAM grants compared to traditional indexed grouping.

qa.q: What is genuinely structurally different about Azure versus AWS for this pipeline, beyond just naming?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Three real differences worth naming explicitly: the Resource Group as a cascading-delete container with no AWS equivalent; the identity model expressed as RBAC role assignments at hierarchy scopes rather than JSON IAM policy documents attached to principals; and ADF/Synapse's more visual, configuration-first design philosophy compared to the more code-first Step Functions/Athena experience on AWS. Everything else -- object storage tiers, managed Spark cost discipline, KQL vs Logs Insights, Grafana's role as the unifying dashboard layer -- is the same concept with a different name.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Cloud control plane APIs orchestrate virtualized hardware, networking (VPC/VNets), IAM policies, and auto-scaling groups.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Overly permissive IAM roles (wildcard actions) or unmonitored resource limits lead to security breaches and unexpected cloud cost spikes.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Serverless/managed services eliminate infrastructure maintenance but introduce cold starts and vendor lock-in.

interviewPlaybook.openingScript: In enterprise cloud environments, Azure capstone -- putting the full stack together must be designed with fault tolerance, zero-downtime deployment pipelines, and explicit security boundaries.
interviewPlaybook.incidentStory: A regional outage threatened pipeline ingestion availability when a dependency failed around Azure capstone -- putting the full stack together. Using infrastructure-as-code and automated failover, I implemented circuit breaking and fallback routing, keeping client payload ingestion at 99.99% availability.

2. Managed Compute (Container / Function) → Orchestration of Azure capstone -- putting the full stack together
3. Persistent Storage / Event Bus (Kafka/S3/DB) → Partitioning & Replication
